# Generated OpenAPI specs

**Do not edit these by hand.** Every file here is generated in its service repo
and synced in; a hand edit is overwritten by the next sync or join.

| File | Source | Generated by |
|---|---|---|
| `public.yaml` | `pythia:api/openapi/public.yaml` | `pythia/scripts/gen-openapi.sh` — swag (v2, OpenAPI 3.1) from the handler annotations |
| `account.yaml` | `atlas:api/openapi/account.yaml` | `node ace openapi:export` from the controller decorators |
| `identity.yaml` | `persona:api/openapi/identity.yaml` | `node ace openapi:export` from the controller decorators |
| `calibri.yaml` | the three above | `scripts/join-specs.sh` — the one document the site renders |

## How a spec gets here

1. **Generate.** Each service's `.githooks/pre-commit` regenerates its spec on
   every commit and stages it if it changed, so the committed spec is never a
   version behind the code. Skip with `SKIP_OPENAPI_HOOK=1`.
2. **Push.** Each service's `.githooks/post-commit` runs
   `scripts/publish_openapi_docs.sh` when the spec changed in that commit. It
   clones this repo with your local git credentials, copies the spec into
   `api-reference/openapi/`, and pushes a `chore: sync … OpenAPI spec` commit.
   Targets come from `DOCS_TARGET_REPOS` (default `calibripredict/docs`); skip
   with `DOCS_SYNC_SKIP=1`, or run the script by hand to retry a failed sync.
3. **Join.** A push that touches `public.yaml`, `account.yaml` or
   `identity.yaml` runs `.github/workflows/join-specs.yml`, which runs
   `scripts/join-specs.sh` to rebuild `calibri.yaml`, the model pages under
   `api-reference/models/` and their navigation group, validates the site with
   `mint validate`, and commits the result.

The specs are committed here rather than fetched at build time because the
service repos are private and Mintlify cannot read them.

## Contract test (pythia)

Several pythia handlers build their response as `map[string]any`, which no
annotation can describe exactly. `pythia:test/contract` checks the published
spec against real responses:

```bash
CONTRACT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8078 go test -tags=contract ./test/contract/...
```

It fails on two things: a documented field whose type has changed, and a public
route added to the server but not to the spec.
